The image shows a mango leaf with numerous small, dark black spots scattered across the leaf surface. The leaf is green but covered with many discrete, small black specks/spots distributed across the lamina.

Key observations:
- Small, discrete dark/black spots scattered across the leaf
- Spots appear raised or superficial (not sunken lesions)
- No obvious white powdery coating
- No large sunken lesions characteristic of anthracnose
- No gall-like blisters
- No brown curling or crumpling
- The black spots appear superficial, like a coating on the surface

This pattern — small black specks distributed superficially across the leaf surface — matches **Sooty Mould**, which forms a black encrustation on leaf surfaces growing on honeydew deposits from sap-feeding insects. The spots are not angular/raised with halos (ruling out Bacterial Canker), not sunken lesions (ruling out Anthracnose), not white powdery (ruling out Powdery Mildew), and not blister-shaped galls (ruling out Gall Midge).
